summary:
Round 12, doc-only, and I checked the test file first: format/src/test/java/binjava/format/SubscriptionEventGrantTest.java is the only staged file under a test path, and its diff touches the class javadoc and the text inside one .as(...) description. Every predicate is byte-identical -- .contains("byteStart=4096"), .contains("byteLen=65536") and the three round-trip cases -- for the seventh round running. NO ASSERTION WEAKENED.

FOUR OF THE FIVE ROUND-11 REPAIRS HOLD, and I re-attacked each rather than reading the summary. (1) K = 1 is now the first entry of the evidence set and the clause names `K > 1 && K <= crossover` as what it exists to red, so an owner who writes that case must assert the bounded path at K = 1 -- two requests, 78,400 + 5,243 bytes -- which reds the mutation and the wiring omission behind it. The false parenthetical 'K = 2 (the smallest bounded share)' is gone and its correction is marked. (3) The sum-based bound is DELETED: the only live byte bound in the cell is now 'by invariant (ii), which is the SPAN', and the sentence that remains carries only the `bytes=byteStart-` job it was written for. I searched the cell for a second statement of the bound and there is none. (5) The K = 2 case at the segment's extremes gives (i)'s 'independent of the run layout' its first layout-varying site and kills `coalesce(ranges, 4 MiB)` at a gap of ~8,383,365. I also checked the extremes placement does not red anything else: at K = 2 the bounded path then fetches 78,400 + ~8,383,365, MORE than the whole object, and no clause forbids that -- 'fewer bytes' is asserted only at K = crossover -- so the case is satisfiable, which is the thing that matters. (4) The assertion form in M5.45h -- at most one `fetchDirectory` and at most one `fetchRange` invocation per (node, segment) -- is the repair verbatim and it reds 2, 64 and 128 alike; 'at most' does not re-admit the zero-fetch coalescer because criterion 1's second half makes all K runs decode their own records.

IT DOES NOT HOLD, ON TWO POINTS, AND BOTH ARE THE REPAIRS THEMSELVES RATHER THAN NEW GROUND. The (iii) repair added the requirement of a second fixture but not the K it must sit at, and ten of the twelve (K, run-size) choices a compliant owner can make leave `sum(byteLen) <= crossover * AVG_RUN_BYTES` -- the survivor the same clause names two lines earlier -- completely green. And the M5.45h repair replaced the binding wording and left the sentence that endorses the retired one: 'CONSTANT-IN-K KILLS EVERY MUTATION THE LITERAL 1 KILLED' is still in the cell, unmarked, two sentences after the cell says constant-in-K is WEAKER than the literal. That sentence is not in HEAD -- it was added by this task and survived the fix to the clause it justifies, which is the half-landed-fix shape this cell itself calls the milestone's most repeated defect.

ONE THING I CONSIDERED AND AM NOT RAISING, so it is not re-derived next round: M5.45h's K = 64 case does not require the 64 deliveries to arrive CONCURRENTLY, so a non-atomic check-then-fetch cache greens a sequential case and issues up to 64 fetches under 64 parallel readNext calls. I dropped it because the tree already owns that scope separately and says so -- SegmentProxy's javadoc: 'WHAT IS STILL TWO READS is two publishes of the same segment that OVERLAP IN TIME: admission happens when a read completes, so both miss and both fetch. That is M5.63.' Raising it here would re-litigate a scope decision that is written down.

findings.location: docs/internal/product/backlog.md:126 (M5.66 criterion 2, 'AND (iii) NEEDS A SECOND FIXTURE AT THE SAME K, NOT ANOTHER K ... Same K, different run sizes, same path is what makes (iii) falsifiable')
findings.title: The second fixture has a shape but no K, and at every K below ~85 it is vacuous: `sum(byteLen) <= crossover * AVG_RUN_BYTES` -- the survivor this very clause names -- agrees with the K-based path at K = 1, 2 and 64 under doubled runs, so the cheapest compliant second fixture kills nothing
findings.failure_scenario: SURVIVING IMPLEMENTATION, unchanged from round 11 because the repair does not reach it: `long budget = crossover * AVG_RUN_BYTES; if (sum(byteLen) <= budget) { header + unionSlice } else { wholeObjectGet }`. It is derived from the recorded crossover, so criterion 1's 'derived, not merely compared' is satisfied in form. WHY THE NEW CLAUSE DOES NOT RED IT. The clause requires 'a second fixture at the SAME K' with 'different run sizes' and 'same path'. It does not say WHICH K, and the sampled set it sits beside is K = 1, 2, 64, crossover, crossover + 1, ~400. Walk all twelve (K, run-size) combinations against the cell's own figures -- 1,600 runs, 8,388,608 bytes, 5,243 bytes per run, crossover 169, budget 169 * 5,243 = 886,067. DOUBLED runs (10,486 bytes): the mutant's switch lands at K = 84, which this clause states itself. K = 1: sum 10,486 <= 886,067, mutant bounded, truth bounded. AGREE, VACUOUS. K = 2: sum 20,972, both bounded. AGREE, VACUOUS. K = 64: sum 671,104 <= 886,067, both bounded. AGREE, VACUOUS. K = 169: sum 1,772,134 > 886,067, mutant WHOLE-OBJECT, truth bounded. RED -- this is one of the two that work. K = 170: mutant whole-object, truth whole-object. AGREE. K ~ 400: agree. HALVED runs (2,621 bytes, mutant switch at K = 338): K = 1, 2, 64, 169 all bounded under both. AGREE. K = 170: mutant bounded (sum 445,570 <= 886,067), truth WHOLE-OBJECT. RED -- the second of the two. K ~ 400: agree. TEN OF TWELVE COMPLIANT CHOICES ARE VACUOUS, and the two that are not are exactly the two round 11 named and this wording dropped: K = crossover with doubled runs, and K = crossover + 1 with halved runs. THE CHOICE AN OWNER ACTUALLY MAKES IS THE VACUOUS ONE. A second fixture is a whole second segment to build; the cheap one to build is small, and 'same K' most naturally means duplicating a case already in the list, of which K = 2 and K = 64 are the two an owner reaches for before the boundary pair, which is already the most expensive pair in the set. Nothing in the clause tells them the boundary is where the proxy disagrees -- the '10,486-byte runs switch at K = 84' figure states the mutant's switch point but never says the fixture must sit ABOVE it. THE HARM IS THE ONE CRITERION 1 EXISTS TO PREVENT, unchanged: at 10,486-byte runs the switch lands at K = 84 rather than the recorded 169, so the measured, ADR-recorded crossover names a K at which the code does not switch anywhere except the one fixture the tests use. AND IT GENERALISES BEYOND MY PROXY: any threshold on a quantity monotone in K -- total recordCount, span/objLen, K * meanRunLen -- disagrees with K only in a band adjacent to the boundary, so a second fixture placed away from the boundary cannot falsify ANY of them, whatever axis it varies. REPAIR, and it is the missing half of the round-11 one: name the two cases. 'at K = crossover with runs of DOUBLE the size the bounded path must STILL run, and at K = crossover + 1 with runs of HALF the size the whole-object path must STILL run' -- the second fixture goes at the boundary pair, because that is the only region where a proxy for K can disagree with K.

findings.location: docs/internal/product/backlog.md:69 (M5.45h criterion 1, '⚠️ CONSTANT-IN-K KILLS EVERY MUTATION THE LITERAL 1 KILLED: a per-run implementation reports 64 or 128 at K = 64, not a constant.')
findings.title: The retired 'constant in K' wording is still endorsed by name two sentences after the cell retires it, unmarked, and an owner who takes that sentence as operative writes the constancy assertion that greens the `(segmentKey, indexId)` cache reporting 2 at K = 64 -- the exact survivor this round's repair was made to red
findings.failure_scenario: TEXTUAL, AND IT IS THE SAME HALF-LANDED SHAPE AS ROUND 11's SUM CLAUSE, ONE ROW OVER. The cell now states the binding form: 'THE COUNT IS ASSERTED AS AT MOST ONE `fetchDirectory` AND AT MOST ONE `fetchRange` INVOCATION PER (NODE, SEGMENT) RATHER THAN AS THE LITERAL 1 FETCH', immediately followed by 'THAT IS AN EQUALITY, NOT A CONSTANCY CLAIM, AND AN EARLIER DRAFT OF THIS CLAUSE SAID "CONSTANT IN K" WITH K = 64 AS ITS ONLY SAMPLE -- WHICH IS WEAKER THAN THE LITERAL IT REPLACED.' One paragraph later, unmarked and in the same imperative ⚠️ voice every binding clause in this cell uses: '⚠️ CONSTANT-IN-K KILLS EVERY MUTATION THE LITERAL 1 KILLED'. The cell asserts a claim and its negation about the same wording, and the negation is the LAST thing it says on the subject. THE SENTENCE IS NEW TO THIS TASK -- `git show HEAD:docs/internal/product/backlog.md | grep -c 'CONSTANT-IN-K KILLS EVERY MUTATION'` returns 0 -- so it was added as the justification for the round-11 draft and survived the repair to the clause it justifies. That is this cell's own diagnosis of the milestone's most repeated defect, applied at the invariant and not at the sentence carrying it, which is verbatim my round-11 major 3 one row over. WHAT THE OWNER WRITES IF THEY TAKE IT AS OPERATIVE: assertThat(fetchCount(K = 64)).isEqualTo(fetchCount(K = 2)), a constancy assertion at two shares. SURVIVING MUTATION UNDER THAT ASSERTION, and it is the one the repair exists to red: the node-scoped owner caches under `(segmentKey, indexId)` rather than `segmentKey`, so a node holding runs of two indices in one segment reports 2 at K = 2 and 2 at K = 64. Constant in K, GREEN, and it is indices-per-node scaling, which non-negotiable 6 forbids by name and which is this row's whole subject. Under the binding form -- at most one `fetchDirectory` and at most one `fetchRange` per (node, segment) -- it reds at 2. The two forms are not equivalent and the cell says so itself, then says the opposite. EVERY OTHER RETIRED WORDING IN THIS CELL AND IN M5.66 IS MARKED ('AN EARLIER DRAFT SAID', 'an earlier version of this cell said', 'The sum clause is deleted rather than annotated'), which is what makes an unmarked one read as live. REPAIR: delete the sentence. It is a pure deletion with nothing left uncovered -- the per-run implementation it argues about is already red under the binding form, which reports 64 invocations of `fetchRange` against at most one -- so it adds no new prose for the next round to find, which is the reason I am naming a deletion rather than a rewording.
